title: Time Leverage
hook: When I stop working, my income stops. That's the real problem I'm trying to solve.
statement: Your time has to multiply. Build things that keep producing after you've done the work once.
explainer: Trading hours one for one caps your income at your calendar. Recorded videos, templates, and documented processes keep working while you're doing something else.
sop: Track a week of hours and tag each as one-for-one or leveraged.
Cut or delegate the lowest value one-for-one tasks first.
Turn one recurring task into a video, template, or written process.
Divide Output by Time on your biggest deliverable and fix the worst ratio.
Reuse old work instead of starting from scratch.
equation_example: Output $8,000, Time 20 hours. $8,000 ÷ 20 = 400, so $400 per hour. Higher means your time produces more without adding hours. Lower means output only grows if your hours do.
question: Name one task you do by hand every time that could become a template or recording.
closing_statement: Make your hours produce after you've stopped working.
caption:
